questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Exploring a new country and university life, as well as academic opportunities

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. The university had an extensive arrival and orientation schedule.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: E-mails from the university and info sessions

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Everything besides selecting courses was pretty easy

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not easy. I lived in an Airbnb, but there are multiple Facebook-groups for off campus housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's of course not the same experience as living on campus, but it's not that bad. Busses to campus are ok but always a bit late. It's possible to bike (unusual for the US).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Incredibly expensive

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Choosing classes before and after your arrival is a bit chaotic.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Before you leave, you have to be ready online at a certain time, and after you arrive the classes you selected online are not guaranteed. You have to "try out" classes, swop them around and e-mail professors a lot. You make your own schedule, so it can be difficult to make the time tables of different classes fit into one schedule.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Student administration in terms of your overall schedule. But when it comes to the individual courses (e.g. if there's one you really want), just email the professors directly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty successful. You just have to be prepared to not get enrolled in every single course you expected/wanted. Be open to take a course in something different, simply because it's the only way to make your time schedule fit. Also Bcourses are nice and fun if you just need an extra ECTS-point or two.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't wait until last minute. Email professors and tell them how much you want to be in their course (even if it seems strange). Be open to try other courses than you expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Excellent courses and professors.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Hard but not too hard. More niche-oriented than at UCPH which is super nice and fun. Amazing and super intelligent professors.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Berkeley demands a lot more reading (every day for every class) than what I'm used to. Also you "have" to speak up in classes. Generally there's a lot more active learning, tasks, assignments, presentations quizzes etc. (all counts in your final grade) than at UCPH, where we're more responsible for our own learning.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Documentary Style, Theorizing the American Film Musical, Japanese Auteurs and Beginner's Guide to the Universe

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I had the pleasure of being taught by Dolores McElroy in Theorizing the American Film Musical. I would recommend any course she teaches, as she is the best professor I've ever had.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: A lot of fees in regards to visa, applications, orientation etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Phone plans are a lot more expensive than in Denmark. Also housing is incredibly expensive, but that was expected. Public transportation to and from campus was free with a Clipper Card though.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Berkeley has a club for literally anything. The big (and serious) "club culture" also means that it can be a bit hard to get accepted into clubs though.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Basically anything you can think of.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was part of Berkeleys Cinematic Arts Club which was nice. People are sweet and the films they make are ambitious.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips! Yosemite, Los Angeles etc. There's a lot of nice cities and hiking opportunites nearby.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not bad. The US is of course culturally different from Denmark, but not too different. I got along with pople fairly easily.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club, show up for events, talk to people in your classes. I made some of my best friends in classes, which was unexpected.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Specifically at Berkeley, students are very ambitious and study a lot. But you kind of get used to it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness of the people. Everyone is super sweet and welcoming. Americans make friends very fast :)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Be prepared to spend A LOT on housing and life in general (and to have a roommate, like in your bedroom). 2. Ask students at UCPH who has previously been on exchange at Berkeley for help. 3. Make the most of your time culturally and socially - the culture of studying all the time can make you think you have to do that as well, but you'll do fine.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look up Facebook-pages for housing and join the UCPH California group too. Ask the people in there for help.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new friends (both international and locals) and experiencing such a high level of education.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Financial problems (I managed because of scholarships - be sure to apply!)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
